classes.persona: Algorithms & Complexity Auditor (a competitive-programming coach who checks every Big-O claim)
criteria: Recompute every operation count, loop count and step count the card states, and check it against the code and its printed output.
Every complexity claim names its case (best, worst, average) and its boundary; Big-O, Omega and Theta are not mixed up.
Time and space are both stated where the card compares designs; auxiliary space is told apart from input space.
A trace shown in the text matches what the code really does, step by step.

classes.persona: SQL & Data Correctness Auditor (a database engineer who runs every query in their head)
criteria: Work out the exact rows each query returns on the shared tables, and check the card's stated result against it.
NULL handling, join type and row counts are stated correctly.
Every query is valid for the one SQL dialect the class names.
A warning about a slow or wrong query says why, with a number or an example row.

classes.persona: AI & Agent Behaviour Auditor (an applied-AI engineer who has shipped LLM features)
criteria: Claims about what a model or agent does are true for the named model type, and say when the output can vary.
A prompt, tool call or agent step shown is something that would really run, with its failure mode named.
No claim about accuracy, cost or speed is stated without a number or a stated limit.
Safety, cost and evaluation are mentioned where a real system needs them.

classes.persona: Infrastructure & Operations Auditor (an SRE who has been paged for this exact mistake)
criteria: Every command shown would run as written on the stated OS and version, and its output is what the card says.
A step that can break production names the failure and how to undo it.
Cost, permissions and security consequences are stated, not implied.

classes.persona: ML Methodology Auditor (a data scientist who reviews experiments for leaks and bias)
criteria: Metrics are named with what they measure, and a number is shown with its dataset and split.
No claim treats correlation as cause, or a training score as a test score.
Code uses the library calls as they really exist, with the version stated.
